dossier_meta.catalog_title: Open Question on Number of Tight Skew Partitions
dossier_meta.statement_text: We do not know how many tight skew partitions there can really be; the authors do not know of a graph with more than linearly many tight skew partitions.
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper shows there are at most $n^3 \log n$ tight skew partitions in an $n$-vertex graph (improving the $n^4$ bound from the Kennedy–Reed list), because for every tight skew partition $(A,B)$ the set $B$ appears at least $k_2^2$ times in the Kennedy–Reed output, where $k_2$ is the size of the second-largest anticomponent of $G[B]$. The true maximum is unknown.
